class LRUCache:
    """
    LRU (Least Recently Used) Cache implementation using a doubly linked list
    and a dictionary for O(1) access.
    
    The most recently used item is kept at the head of the linked list,
    and the least recently used item is at the tail. When the cache is full,
    the tail node is evicted.
    """

    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Capacity must be positive")
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.cache = {}  # key -> Node
        # Dummy head and tail to simplify edge cases
        self.head = Node()  # dummy head
        self.tail = Node()  # dummy tail
        self.head.next = self.tail
        self.tail.prev = self

The dust in the archives didn’t smell like decay; it smelled like dry paper and old glue. Elias, the head archivist, preferred it that way. It was a scent that implied permanence, a quiet promise that things would stay exactly where they were left.

He was processing a return from the "Unclaimed" bin when he found the first note. It was tucked into the spine of a 1994 edition of *The History of the Great Plague*. The paper was yellowed, the ink a faded blue ballpoint.

*Page 42. The description of the rats is inaccurate. They didn’t just die; they fled. Look at the footnotes.*

Elias frowned. He opened the book. The note was tucked between pages 41 and 42. He checked the footnotes. There was nothing there. Just standard citations. He slid the note into his pocket, assuming it was a prank by a bored student, or perhaps a leftover from a previous owner who had marked their place.

Three days later, he found another. This one was in a copy of *Marx’s Capital*, Volume I.
